observed_descriptive_result.primary_endpoint: Pack E has the higher pooled T+15 directional accuracy: 113/252 (0.448413) versus Pack A 87/208 (0.418269).
observed_descriptive_result.common_pair_check: On the 206 common paired-scoreable observations, Pack E is 100/206 (0.485437) and Pack A is 86/206 (0.417476); A-E is -0.067961.
observed_descriptive_result.other_endpoints: Pack E has lower magnitude interval error and higher T+5, T+30, T+60, and path accuracy. Pack A has higher reversal accuracy, so the descriptive pattern is not uniform across every authorized endpoint.
observed_descriptive_result.coverage: Pack E has 7 no-signal exclusions and Pack A has 51. This establishes a large difference in directional coverage and selectivity, not a coverage-adjusted quality score.

scientific_inference: The record supports moderate descriptive evidence favoring Pack E on the primary endpoint and several supporting endpoints. It does not establish statistical significance, causality, general superiority, or a winner.
unsupported_speculation: Pack E is proven superior to Pack A.
A provider should be selected or weighted from these results.
A meta-forecast or new Pack design is justified by these results alone.
future_hypothesis: A separately authorized paired inferential comparison of the existing 206 common T+15-scoreable pairs can test whether the observed descriptive gap is compatible with a stable Pack-level difference. A separate coverage analysis can assess the no-signal asymmetry without changing the current metric contract.
immediate_impulse: Immediate Impulse directional accuracy remains NOT_APPLICABLE_STRICT because there are zero SUPPORTED Outcomes. It cannot corroborate or qualify the T+15 result in Round 1.
conclusion: Continue Pack E development as a hypothesis-supported arm while retaining Pack A as the baseline comparator. Do not replace Pack A or redesign the Packs on this descriptive evidence alone.
